segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He went into a synagogue again, and a man was there who had a withered hand.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They were watching him closely to see whether he would heal him on the Sabbath, so that they could bring a charge against him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to the man with the withered hand,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Get up and stand in the middle.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do harm, to save a life or to kill?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But they were silent.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He looked around at them with anger, deeply grieved at the hardness of their hearts, and said to the man,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Stretch out your hand.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He stretched it out, and his hand was restored.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The Pharisees went out and immediately began plotting against him with the Herodians, how they might destroy him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus withdrew with his disciples to the sea, and a great multitude from Galilee followed; and from Judea

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and from Jerusalem and from Idumea and beyond the Jordan and around Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, hearing all that he was doing, came to him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He told his disciples to keep a small boat ready for him because of the crowd, so that they would not crush him;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for he had healed many, so that all who had afflictions were falling upon him to touch him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the unclean spirits, whenever they saw him, would fall down before him and cry out,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “You are the Son of God!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he warned them sternly not to make him known.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he went up the mountain and called to him those whom he himself wanted, and they came to him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He appointed twelve, so that they would be with him and so that he could send them out to proclaim

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and to have authority to drive out the demons.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He appointed the twelve: Simon, to whom he gave the name Peter;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and James the son of Zebedee and John the brother of James (to them he gave the name Boanerges, which means Sons of Thunder);

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and Andrew and Philip and Bartholomew and Matthew and Thomas and James the son of Alphaeus and Thaddaeus and Simon the Cananaean

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and Judas Iscariot, who also handed him over.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he went into a house, and the crowd gathered again, so that they could not even eat bread.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When his family heard of it, they went out to take hold of him, for they were saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “He is out of his mind.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem were saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “He has Beelzebul,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “By the ruler of the demons he drives out the demons.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So he called them to him and spoke to them in parables:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “How can Satan drive out Satan?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And if a house is divided against itself, that house will not be able to stand.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And if Satan has risen up against himself and is divided, he cannot stand; his end has come.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But no one can go into the strong man’s house and plunder his goods unless he first ties up the strong man; and then he will plunder his house.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly I tell you, everything will be forgiven the sons of men, the sins and the blasphemies, whatever blasphemies they utter;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit never has forgiveness, but is guilty of an eternal sin.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said this because they were saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “He has an unclean spirit.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then his mother and his brothers came, and standing outside, they sent word to him, calling for him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A crowd was sitting around him, and they said to him,

segments.speaker: crowd
segments.text: “Look, your mother and your brothers are outside, looking for you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Who are my mother and my brothers?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And looking around at those seated in a circle around him, he said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Here are my mother and my brothers!

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For whoever does the will of God, that person is my brother and sister and mother.”

notes.note: The Herodians were apparently supporters of the family of Herod, here Herod Antipas, who ruled Galilee under Rome. Little else is known of them. Their alliance with the Pharisees is striking, since the two groups had little in common politically or religiously.

Some early manuscripts add “whom he also named apostles” after “twelve”; the edition translated here judges this an addition under the influence of Luke 6:13. The repeated “He appointed the twelve” in verse 16 is likewise missing from many manuscripts.

The verb describes what a herald does: making a public announcement on someone else's authority. “Preach” now suggests delivering a sermon to a congregation, so “proclaim” is used, as in several modern versions. Many translations still have “preach.”

notes.traditional: Simon the Canaanite; Simon the Cananaean; Simon the Zealot
notes.note: The epithet has nothing to do with Canaan or the village of Cana. It represents an Aramaic word meaning “zealous one,” which Mark leaves untranslated and Luke renders in Greek as “the Zealot.” Whether it marks religious zeal in general or sympathy with armed resistance to Rome is uncertain.

The verb is the ordinary word for handing someone or something over, and it is the same word used later when Jesus is handed over to the chief priests and to Pilate. Most translations render it “betrayed” when Judas is the subject, which fits what he did but hides the repeated verb. Greek had a separate word for treachery, which Mark does not use here.

notes.traditional: his friends (KJV); his family (most modern versions)
notes.note: The Greek is a vague phrase, literally “those from beside him,” which can mean relatives, associates or envoys. Most scholars take it as his relatives, because his mother and brothers arrive in verse 31. It is also possible to read “they were saying” impersonally, so that the family acts because people were saying he was out of his mind.

In the Gospels “scribes” are not copyists but trained experts in the Law of Moses and its interpretation, recognised as teachers and legal authorities. Those “from Jerusalem” carry the weight of the religious capital. Some translations render the word “teachers of the law.”

Beelzebul is a name for the chief of the demons, treated in verse 23 as equivalent to Satan. Its origin is debated; it probably goes back to a title of the Canaanite god Baal. The form “Beelzebub” in older English Bibles comes from the Latin tradition and echoes the god of Ekron in 2 Kings 1.

This is a Semitic idiom meaning simply human beings, men and women alike; it is the plural of the expression “son of man.” Some modern versions render it “people.” The idiom is kept here because the Greek has it.

Later manuscripts replace “sin” with “judgment,” which is the source of the King James Version's “eternal damnation.” The earlier and harder reading is “sin.” The phrase means a sin whose guilt is never removed, matching “never has forgiveness” in the same sentence.

Some manuscripts add “and your sisters” here. The edition translated here omits the words; other critical editions print them in brackets as doubtful. They may have been added because of “sister” in verse 35, or dropped to match verses 31 and 33–34.

The Greek plural can include women, and this translation normally renders it “brothers and sisters” when a mixed group is meant, as the seated crowd is here. “Brothers” is kept because Jesus is repeating word for word the phrase just used of his actual mother and brothers in verses 32–33, and the echo is the point of the saying. Verse 35 then names “sister” explicitly.
